title: Whispered Scrolls: I'm building a MMO with AI tools. Here's where the AI helps, where it hurts, and how I optimize my workflow to deliver value!
author: RillyBoss
selftext:
I'm a solo dev building Whispered Scrolls. It's currently released as a playable alpha, and I'm ready to open it up to the public.

**Where AI is helping:** systems and scaffolding (skill logic, quest structure, boss phases) and fast iteration. I could try an idea and have it running the same day. I have built in game reporting that captures screenshots, game state, and more, that allows for rapid bug fixing. AI has also allowed me to build advanced testing, building harnesses that allow me to sim combat, dungeons, gathering, etc and capture real metrics to make data driven decisions.

**Where AI hurts:** maps, spawn placement, models, and balance. All of the art is procedural, as is the engine. I've leveraged AI to help build a world map off my specification, layout resources and nodes, create graphics, etc. From there, I built editors for maps, models, quests, and equipment. The initial workflow is often deeply in need of more polish, which my tooling allows me to add a human touch on any aspect without relying on AI.

**A real example from balance:** I ran simulated party fights. At 2x trash damage, a party with no healer barely struggled, so I raised the damage to 3x and 4.5x. The simulation caught a gap, but it didn't replace playtesting.

**Procedural art:** every model, texture and sound is generated in code, so AI tools touch the systems and the content, not an art pack.

**Question for the sub:** how are you keeping AI-generated content consistent across a large game? I'm especially interested in quest and lore consistency.

Play: [https://whisperedscrolls.com](https://whisperedscrolls.com) (playable on windows via download or your browser, Chrome works best)

comments.author: testus_maximus
comments.body:
Check out https://github.com/levy-street/world-of-claudecraft and see if they already made something that you can re-use or in other ways find useful.  

Actually, with how much AI gamedev is going on these days, there should probably be more places that list similar open source projects, so that either people or agents have the option to use a foundation instead of starting from scratch.

replies.author: RillyBoss
replies.body: I've been following this project for a while! I actually read through their codebase around the time it was released. They've definitely got a cool project on their hands and I think it's a neat resource for people willing to learn from it!
